title: PR review scratchpad - runtime batching & cache
body:
Context: quick dump after a first pass of PR #1427 (batching + KV cache tweaks). Meant to be a messy checklist for follow-ups, not a final review.

High level impression:
- PR moves batching window from 8ms -> 5ms for low-latency tier; hopeful perf wins for short sequences but risk of smaller effective batch sizes during peak.
- Introduces a new "evict-on-shift" KV policy to reduce memory pressure, plus small refactor of kv_cache::lookup.
- Good test coverage for happy paths, missing a couple of edge cases around concurrent eviction + refill.

Quick checklist (for final review):
- [ ] Confirm perf numerics: run 1k warmup + 10k steady for seq_len 32/128 on p3/rtx6000 to measure tail latency (p50/p95/p99). Compare old vs new batching window.
- [ ] Add microbenchmark for effective batch size distribution (histogram) to ensure 5ms doesn't collapse batch to singletons under realistic qps.
- [ ] Validate memory usage with long-running load test (24h) with heavy KV churn; signal if GC/eviction spikes.
- [ ] Unit tests for concurrent eviction path: simulate thread A evicting entry X while thread B tries to read and then repopulate. Ensure no use-after-free.
- [ ] Add comment explaining rationale for 5ms; link to issue INF-4821 in code (so future readers can find design notes).

Refactor suggestions (non-blocking but helpful):
- kv_cache::lookup currently returns optional<Handle>. Consider returning a small RAII wrapper that tags whether entry is pinned; that would make lifetime semantics explicit in callers. Could reduce subtle bugs in serving-runtime/cache_manager.cpp.
- batching scheduler: split heuristics into two funcs: should_flush_by_latency(now, oldest) and should_flush_by_capacity(batch). Right now both inlined; splitting improves testability and makes it easier to A/B different heuristics.
- Replace raw mutex in cache_eviction with a slimmer reader-writer lock for reads-heavy workloads. Quick experiment: rwlock vs mutex on local benchmark for 64 threads read/1 write.

Edge cases and questions to follow up: 
- What happens when a request is routed to a downgraded model variant during a batch? There is mention of "fallback when capacity constrained" in comments but no explicit abort/translate path in batch assembly code. Need tests where route policy triggers fallback mid-batching.
- Evict-on-shift: does it evict entries that are still in-flight for another request? Need deterministic interleaving tests.
- Is the new eviction policy compatible with persistent cache dump/restore? The PR touches the serialization code briefly but I didn't see migration logic for older snapshot formats.

Specific code notes (line pointers from PR diff):
- serving/runtime/batching/scheduler.cpp +87: tight loop that polls waiting queue; minor nit: add a small exponential backoff jitter to avoid thundering herd when under extreme contention.
- serving/runtime/cache/kv_cache.cpp +201: lookup() returns raw pointer then release() call at +228; looks fragile if an exception thrown in between — but serving runtime compiled with -fno-exceptions normally, still safer to use RAII wrapper as suggested above.
- serving/runtime/telemetry/metrics.cpp +42: new metric kv_evictions_total introduced; good — add a complementary kv_repop_total to track thrash.

Test suggestions to add to PR: 
- concurrency tests: use tsan build target and a deterministic scheduler harness to reproduce race scenarios for eviction+read. Document steps to reproduce.
- integration test: simulate model fallback (use fake router) and ensure batch assembled uses homogeneous model variants or triggers split flush.
- golden snapshot test for serialized cache: roundtrip old snapshot -> load -> save -> compare hash to ensure migration doesn't silently drop metadata.

Follow-ups / Owners (proposal):
- Perf runs and batch histograms: Diego Morales (assign INF-4821-1)
- Concurrency unit tests + tsan repro: Lena Park (INF-4821-2)
- Add comments and link to INF-4821 in code: Omar Singh (I'll do a small PR patch)
- Serialization migration tests: engineering infra team (ping @sre-tools)

Random notes to self (scratch):
- When measuring p99, ensure tail noise filtered (CI machine noisy), redo on dedicated bench infra.
- Consider an opt-in config flag for the 5ms window behind a feature flag (default off) so we can A/B in prod.
- Might be worth adding a quick histogram metric: batching_window_effective_ms to see actual waiting time per batch.

Slack snippets to paste into PR comment (informal):
"Quick pass: looks promising but we need concurrency tests for eviction paths and perf histograms to be comfortable with 5ms default. I'll add a small RAII wrapper for kv handles in a follow-up and Diego can run the bench numbers. Thanks for the clean diff!"

Unresolved decisions (call them out):
- Default 5ms vs 8ms: keep experimental flag or flip default? (ops wants lower tail latencies, infra worried about CPU cost)
- Eviction semantics when fallback routing occurs mid-batch: conservative approach is to flush batch early; aggressive is to keep trying to assemble homogeneous batch and let router drop requests — need product/plat signal.

Bottom line: PR is a big step, but we must harden concurrency and add observability (batch histograms + repop/evict counters) before merging to main branch. Plan: add tests + perf artifacts, then signoff.

--- end of scratchpad ---

(NOTE: messy and incomplete on purpose — saved from local workstation, will clean up when adding tests/bench results.)
